text: The actual checks confirm the unchanged analog design and retain the four intrinsic J1 findings. I will now write the future-work plan, record the measurement/fault/order holds, and read back the documents before the original finish gate. No physical result or order will be marked complete.

args.content:
# Development and bring-up plan: protected USB-C 500 mA prototype

## 1. Status, scope and evidence boundary

Stage 8 planning, 2026-10-09: docs/DEVPLAN.md defines the ordered bring-up, existing-pad probe map, acceptance/evidence matrix, unresolved risks and approval-gated prototype order plan. This is documentation of future work only: no prototype has been ordered, manufactured, assembled, energized or physically tested in this pipeline. Every physical test is NOT RUN and every release hold remains open. The original finish gate decides software-stage acceptance; plan completion is not hardware qualification.

The required targets remain 4.75-5.25 V at VBUS input; 500 mA TOTAL continuous external load, available on J2 alone, J3 alone or shared; strictly less than 2 mA steady unloaded VBUS current; fitted-component BOM strictly below USD 8 per board at Q100; board envelope no larger than 40 x 30 mm, two 1 oz copper layers and nominal 1.6 mm FR-4. The assumed environment is dry indoor 0-50 C, no enclosure or coating, with ESD-controlled handling. No USB data, PD negotiation, voltage conversion, reverse-feed capability, MCU or radio is specified.

Rationale: a useful plan preserves every target and marks evidence gaps rather than turning them into apparent passes.

### Actual Stage 8 software evidence

The validated proposal is plan-protected-500ma-bringup-v21. Fresh native readback of schematic.intent.json and list_symbols confirms ten fitted parts: J1/J2/J3/U1/R1/R2/R4/C1/C2/D1. The intent has six functional nets: VBUS_RAW, +5V_PROTECTED, GND, CC1, CC2 and LED_A. list_nets also returns PWR_FLAG, which is schematic power metadata, not a fitted component or extra power path. verify_symbols reports 11 definitions matching installed libraries or exact engine power templates with no divergences. Fresh ERC and BOM/PINOUT drift are clean. Fresh legibility reports zero errors and one low-utilization advisory (0.29 occupied fraction versus advisory threshold 0.5); this unchanged advisory does not require a hardware edit.

Fresh native run_drc reports clean for its original placement/routing gate and separately retains four intrinsic J1 hole_clearance findings. The documented independent Stage 5 raw KiCad result on this unchanged board has four errors at 0.1944 mm versus the unchanged 0.2500 mm limit, exit 5, and zero unconnected items. That independent raw check is historical and was not repeated in Stage 8. The findings are not repaired, suppressed or waived by this plan. Native draft-stage acceptance is not raw-zero DRC or fabrication clearance.

firmware/README.md was read back and records no programmable components and the analog/passive operating reason. Firmware remains NOT APPLICABLE; no build, flashing step, pins.h, dummy code or unavailable-toolchain claim is introduced. The inherited U1 description inside the generated symbol remains a limitation: fitted U1 is TPS2065CDBVR; embedded TPS2051C parent prose is not a rating source. Correct the engine inheritance through a supported workflow before standalone library reuse.

The prior Stage 6 package is a source-bound review artifact with manufacturerAcceptance=not-verified. Stage 8 changes no PCB, schematic, project settings, intent, BOM or generated export. Read docs/OUTPUTS.md for exact file paths, hashes and integrity rules. Any later source change requires fresh original gates and regenerated exports; never hand-edit a manifest or export to force consistency. No visual 3D/Gerber review, new quote, manufacturer approval or physical result is claimed here.

Rationale: fresh tool checks, historical checks, manufacturer evidence, conditional calculations and future measurements have different meanings.

## 2. Hold points and sequence

The roles below are proposed responsibilities, not assigned people or commitments. The project owner approves scope/spend; the electrical reviewer closes operating/fault evidence; the PCB/assembly reviewer closes manufacturability; the fabricator confirms its process; the bench operator records tests and immediately stops unsafe work.

1. H0, before quotation/upload or ordering: review the exact current revision, risk register and sources. Resolve the four raw J1 errors with a supported engineering change or fully documented engineering/fabricator disposition; do not silently relax the 0.2500 mm rule. Confirm J3 finished plated holes of 0.97-1.07 mm, connector/IC drawing overlays, manual solder feasibility, actual outline interpretation, current-path geometry and safe fixture access. Current state: OPEN. A quotation is not manufacturing approval.
2. H1, before procurement/fabrication: independently review the final generated package and exact source hashes, actual front/back/3D views and all software reports. Obtain itemized quotes and lead times, review the order details, then obtain explicit user approval. Current state: OPEN, no order placed. All known unresolved safety/manufacturing issues must be disposed of for this limited engineering sample; later bench-dependent performance claims remain unqualified.
3. H2, before first power: inspect the received bare board, reconcile fabricated geometry and parts against the approved revision, assemble and inspect one board, complete unpowered checks and approve the normal-power test fixture. Current state: NOT RUN.
4. H3, before normal-load/corner qualification: pass initial room-temperature unloaded screening, then establish the current measurement method, thermal monitoring, capable source/cable and external load configuration. Current state: NOT RUN.
5. H4, before any deliberate overload/short: meet the exact-device and fixture/energy prerequisites below and approve the individual fault-test run sheet. Current state: BLOCKED pending review, not a fault-test failure.
6. H5, before any production/release claim: close all required electrical, fault, recovery, visibility, mechanical, assembly, sourcing and uncertainty evidence; retest changes; review sample limitations and sign a release decision. Current state: OPEN. Passing three prototypes is not a production reliability or regulatory qualification.

Rationale: manufacture of a specifically approved engineering sample and later hardware qualification are separate decisions; this document authorizes neither.

## 3. What to meter first and where to probe

There are no dedicated TP footprints in the ten-part design. The following are existing pad/contact locations, not newly added test points. Use insulated micro-grabbers or a reviewed fixture and confirm access while unpowered. Clip ground first to a verified GND pad; do not hand-probe adjacent SOT-23 or USB fine-pitch pins when a safer capacitor/connector pad exposes the same net. Never assume a symbol's left/right drawing is the actual board orientation.

| Signal / purpose | Existing probe locations from current intent | First expected observation / caution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GND reference | J2.2; J3.2 or J3.4; C1.2; C2.2; U1.2; D1.1; J1 ground/shield | With source disconnected, verify continuity between these locations and identify separate source-return and load-return sense points. Ground-path drops matter under load. |
| VBUS_RAW input | Prefer C1.1; U1.5 IN and U1.4 EN; J1 A4/A9/B4/B9 | First live voltage, measured to local GND at the board, must stay 4.75-5.25 V in normal tests. EN is directly connected; do not lift or drive it. |
| +5V_PROTECTED output | Prefer C2.1 or J2.1; J3.1/J3.3; U1.1; R4.1 | Second live voltage: positive and tracking input minus path losses, with no bypass. No exact regulated 5 V minimum is specified. |
| LED_A | R4.2 or D1.2 anode | Measure only after the two rails are correct. D1 cathode is pin 1 to GND. Measure R4 voltage to estimate LED current using the measured resistor value and instrument uncertainty. |
| CC1 | R1.1 and J1.A5 | Source/cable absent: nominal 5.1 kohm to GND through R1. Never join to CC2. |
| CC2 | R2.1 and J1.B5 | Source/cable absent: nominal 5.1 kohm to GND through R2. Between CC1 and CC2 about 10.2 kohm through the two Rd paths is expected, not an open circuit. |
| Whole-board VBUS input current | Series measurement in the fixture's VBUS feed to J1; sense voltage at C1.1/C1.2 | Measure only VBUS board demand, with both outputs open for idle. Account for meter burden and avoid including fixture electronics or CC supply current. A whole-board reading already includes LED, U1 and leakage. |
| External load currents and voltage drop | Separate calibrated loads/meters at J2.1/2 and J3 positive/ground pairs | Sum external load currents to 500 mA; do not count board overhead as external delivery or rely on equal sharing of parallel header pins. Use Kelvin voltage sensing where practical. |

Current component-side placement from docs/LAYOUT.md: J2 is rotated 180 degrees; positive pad 1 is at (134,106) mm on the right and GND pad 2 at (130.5,106) on the left. J3 positive pads 1/3 form the left column X=135.2 mm; ground pads 2/4 form the right column X=137.74 mm, rows Y=117/119.54. D1 cathode pad 1 is (131.5,125) and anode pad 2 (128.96,125). Verify the actual fabricated revision and visible markings before attaching a lead. Do not infer mating-plug polarity from these component-side coordinates.

U1.3 FLT and J1 data/SBU pins A6/A7/A8/B6/B7/B8 are intentional no-connects. No added FLT pull-up, external EN bias resistor, R3 or ILIM_SET is required. Do not connect them merely to obtain an oscilloscope status signal; that would change the circuit and current ledger.

Rationale: use the real pin/net contract and accessible existing pads without inventing a test connector or modifying a generated design.

## 4. Equipment and record setup

Prepare, inspect and record before use: adjustable regulated 5 V supply with adjustable current/energy limit and fast accessible cutoff; a correctly wired USB-C source fixture with appropriate source-side CC behavior and a known-capable cable; calibrated low-current DMM or shunt/measurement amplifier with known burden, offset, resolution and uncertainty; a second DMM for local rail voltages; two calibrated electronic loads or reviewed resistor fixtures; oscilloscope with suitable voltage/current probes and adequate transient bandwidth; temperature sensors or characterized IR method; dry controlled-temperature setup for 0/25/50 C work; microscope, ESD mat, insulated fixture, nonflammable work surface and suitable guarded fault switch/load fixture.

The source/fixture must supply 500 mA external load plus board overhead and startup demand. Rd only establishes attachment; the board does not sense advertised current or negotiate PD. Do not use a laptop port as an uncharacterized fault source. No mains-side construction is required. Confirm scope-ground connections cannot short a rail or defeat a current shunt; use appropriate differential measurement rather than floating protective earth. Set loads to non-sourcing behavior and verify zero backfeed with input off. Never put an ammeter directly across a supply.

For every run record board serial/revision and source hashes; fitted part/lot/substitution status; operator/date; instrument model/serial/calibration and ranges; fixture diagram; source/cable identity; current-limit setting; actual VBUS at the board; ambient, board/case temperatures and soak stability; connector/orientation/load split; sample rate/bandwidth; raw readings/waveforms/photos; uncertainty; acceptance rule; result and anomaly/stop reason. Keep observed values separate from calculations and expected limits. Record NOT RUN until actual execution, INCONCLUSIVE for a setup-limited result, and FAIL for a demonstrated requirement violation.

Rationale: a test is reproducible only when its conditions and uncertainty can be reconstructed.

## 5. Ordered bring-up procedure

All numbered steps below are future work and currently NOT RUN. Stop at the first unmet hold or unexplained result. The source remains disconnected for steps 1-3.

### Step 1: received-board and assembly inspection

After H0/H1 and receipt, measure finished board outline/thickness and verify the approved two-layer, copper/plating and FR-4 process. Inspect all holes, slots, annuli and J1 NPTH/contact clearances; verify the fabricator's J3 finished-hole evidence rather than equating a 1.00 mm nominal drill with a tolerance guarantee. Test exact connectors for insertion, board-edge/plug fit and accessible contacts before soldering.

Assemble one board first using the exact BOM: TPS2065CDBVR, USB4105-GF-A, Phoenix 1984617, Harwin M20-9980246, the two 5.1k resistors, 10k R4, two 1uF capacitors and WP710A10LID. Check U1 pin-1/package identity and D1 cathode. Inspect USB fine-pitch bridges/opens and anchors, all five U1 leads, THT barrel fill and LED lead stress. Verify adequate J2 torque support, connector mating clearance and unkeyed-header labeling. Follow exact manufacturer solder limits; the LED's manual-solder repair/rework guidance is a process qualification issue, not an initial-assembly endorsement. Clean flux with a compatible process and dry fully. Photograph both sides.

Acceptance: assembly matches the approved source and manufacturer geometry/process conditions, no visible bridge/missing joint/reversed part, mechanical access and markings reviewed. Any deviation is a rework/review hold. Rationale: a correct file cannot identify an assembly error.

### Step 2: first meter checks, unpowered

Disconnect USB, supply, loads and scope; discharge capacitors through a suitable resistor and verify near-zero rail voltage with a voltmeter before switching to resistance/continuity. First identify GND at J2.2 and verify intended ground returns. Then check VBUS_RAW-to-GND and +5V_PROTECTED-to-GND for an unexplained persistent near-short, allowing capacitor charging and semiconductor/LED polarity effects. Record both lead polarities if needed; there is no justified universal resistance threshold for these populated rails. A continuity beep alone cannot diagnose the switch path.

Verify all documented same-net pad connections with a low-energy meter: J1 VBUS contacts to C1.1/U1.5/U1.4; U1.1 to C2.1/J2.1/J3.1/J3.3/R4.1; each ground return. Inspect/test for unintended copper/solder bypass of U1, but do not demand infinite resistance between input and output of a semiconductor switch. Compare direction-dependent observations with exact-device behavior and the bare-board continuity review. Verify J2/J3 polarity and LED diode orientation.

Measure each Rd at R1.1/R2.1 to GND with source/cable absent. At reference temperature, 5.1k +/-1% is 5.049-5.151 kohm before meter error; consider TCR, actual temperature and any fixture loading. CC1-to-CC2 should show the series path around 10.2k, not a direct short. Verify continuity of each CC pin to its own resistor only. Check R4 against 10k +/-1% with an appropriate in-circuit method or preassembly measurement; do not desolder solely to make a questionable in-circuit reading look ideal.

Acceptance: intended continuity, separate CC networks, correct parts/polarity and no unexplained shorts/opens. Rationale: these low-energy checks find destructive mistakes before power is applied.

### Step 3: prepare the live fixture and stop limits

Confirm H2, secure the board and insulated probes while unpowered. Initially leave J2/J3 externally open. Set the source for measured 5.00 V at the board and use a proposed 10 mA initial screening limit; this is a reversible engineering test setting, not the product current limit or a guarantee that all startup surges fit it. Review fixture capacitance and cutoff response first. If startup enters current limit, switch off and characterize the cause with a reviewed setup before changing that setting; a clipped startup is INCONCLUSIVE, not an automatic board failure or permission to raise the limit blindly.

Any wrong polarity, solder bridge, unexplained steady rail-to-ground low resistance, out-of-range input, instrument/fixture overrating, unexpected current limiting, smoke/odor/discoloration, rapidly rising temperature or exceeded reviewed temperature/energy limit requires immediate source isolation and discharge verification before investigation. Do not probe resistance on a powered board, move series-current wiring while energized, backfeed either output, parallel supplies, bypass U1 or enlarge a protection limit merely to force a pass.

Rationale: modest initial energy limits reduce consequence while the board's identity and rail behavior are being confirmed.

### Step 4: first power, unloaded at room temperature

Energize briefly under observation. Meter C1.1 to C1.2 first, then C2.1 to C2.2, then J2/J3 polarity. Confirm U1 EN follows VBUS_RAW and the protected rail is positive without abnormal heating. Check LED_A and D1 only after the rails are correct. Observe LED visibility and input current; do not assume the expected approximately 0.33 mA LED estimate or 0.831 mA allocation is the reading. Capture turn-on rails/current if possible without violating the reviewed energy limits. Disconnect and discharge before changing wiring.

Acceptance for this screen: correct rail/polarity behavior, no unexplained limiting/heating and settled idle evidence consistent with the strict target after uncertainty. A good single room-temperature reading is only an initial screen. Rationale: diagnose input, then protected output, then indicator in that order.

### Step 5: close the unloaded-current and visibility evidence

Whole-board unloaded VBUS acceptance requires the measured steady-state current plus its documented expanded uncertainty to be strictly below 2.000 mA with both external outputs open and U1 enabled, throughout the required 4.75-5.25 V and assumed dry 0-50 C envelope. Count every VBUS-fed path once; measure source-CC demand separately. The 0.831 mA ledger remains conditional. Corner/sample tests alone do not prove all temperature, tolerance, aging or production extremes; close the remaining range-wide analysis and evidence before qualification.

Use calibrated ranges with suitable resolution and low burden; record local input voltage during current measurement. If the reading is near the limit or unstable, improve measurement accuracy and investigate rather than round down. Use 4.75, 5.00 and 5.25 V at 0, 25 and 50 C as the proposed minimum engineering characterization matrix; record actual achieved values and uncertainty, add intermediate sweep points where behavior is non-monotonic, and use dry conditioning to avoid condensation at 0 C. Wait for documented thermal/current stability; elapsed time alone is not equilibrium. Repeat measurements on the available independent assemblies and after fault/rework stress, without claiming statistical lot coverage.

Reconcile the conditional ledger: LED 0.540 mA; U1 IN bias 0.190 mA including an unproven 0.100 mA reserve above the 0.090 mA IOUT=0 specification; separate EN 0.001 mA; C1/C2 0.050 mA; board/connectors 0.050 mA; absent external pull-ups and other loads 0. Sum 0.831 mA, conditional margin 1.169 mA. Whole-board current already contains these paths. A branch investigation on a separate approved fixture may identify their bounds; never add extracted branch currents again to the same measured total. Do not remove LED/capacitors to call that the required unloaded configuration. Close exact capacitor effective capacitance over bias/tolerance/temperature/aging and leakage, LED-loaded U1 bias, and board cleanliness/humidity dependence separately.

At 4.75 V and intended viewing conditions, verify the protected LED is visibly useful; record ambient illumination, viewing distance/angle, temperature and observer acceptance agreed before testing. Check the corners too. The LED's 2 mA optical data does not guarantee its approximately 0.3 mA application point. If R4 or D1 must change, use a new approved design change and recompute the full current budget; do not silently sacrifice the strict idle limit.

Acceptance: uncertainty-inclusive idle current below 2 mA at every qualified condition, a justified range-wide tolerance/temperature envelope, closed leakage/bias evidence and agreed visible indication. Anything missing remains UNKNOWN/INCONCLUSIVE. Rationale: finite prototype samples and nominal arithmetic cannot prove a guaranteed worst case.

### Step 6: normal 500 mA delivery, voltage drop and temperature

After H3, use a reviewed source/current setting adequate for load plus overhead and startup without masking a fault. Ramp external load through 0, 100, 250 and 500 mA at room temperature while recording local VBUS, protected voltage, each connector voltage/current, source limiting and temperatures. Maintain 500 mA TOTAL external load; the LED and protection demand are additional source current. Test J2 alone; J3 alone; and shared splits 250/250, 100/400 and 400/100 mA. Check each usable J3 positive/ground pair individually at the full required load so no assumption of equal contact sharing conceals a weak path.

Repeat the required full-load configurations across the voltage/ambient matrix, both USB plug orientations and relevant source/cable combinations. Allow thermal stabilization and document a continuous-load dwell chosen before execution, initially proposed as at least 30 minutes after stabilization; extend if temperatures continue drifting. The dwell is a characterization choice, not proof of indefinite reliability. Verify measured delivery reaches the required 500 mA after considering load/current uncertainty; the engineer should define any small guard band before test rather than silently reducing the requested load.

Measure local drops across the input connector/return, U1 IN-to-OUT, distribution copper/return and each output contact/mating path. The sourced 154 milliohm U1 maximum implies about 77.10 mV and 38.60 mW at conditional switched load 500.640 mA under its table conditions. This is not a whole-board voltage guarantee. Approximately 4.67290 V at 4.75 V input is switch-only; other copper/contact drops are still unknown. Record the actual output minimum and accept it against the unchanged unregulated contract and reviewed component/path limits, not an invented regulated 5 V specification.

Acceptance: 500 mA external delivery on each required configuration without nuisance limit, loss of connection or uncontrolled temperature; valid source/cable operation; all component/current/temperature ratings maintained, including a defensible U1 junction-temperature estimate within its stated range. A case-temperature reading alone does not prove TJ <=125 C. Unexplained loss or heating requires redesign/retest. Rationale: a 1 A switch rating and wide traces do not qualify the assembled path.

### Step 7: USB orientation, startup/inrush and load transients

Verify CC1/CC2 separation and normal attachment with both plug orientations on a known-capable source/cable. Record source advertisement/fixture behavior and cable identity. Rd does not establish an arbitrary 500 mA-plus-overhead entitlement. No USB data or PD function is expected. Capture startup at no external load and at reviewed representative loads/capacitances, input extremes and relevant ambient corners. Record C1/C2 effective-value evidence and every external capacitance; there is no declared unlimited capacitive-load capability.

Measure VBUS sag/overshoot, protected-rail rise/overshoot, peak/duration of input current and stable operation after 0-to-500 mA and release steps. Distinguish source protection from U1 limiting; source-clipped data cannot prove the device's unrestricted response. Test no-backfeed fixture behavior with source off, but do not intentionally externally power a product output to claim reverse blocking. Record common-rail impact on both outputs and LED.

Acceptance: stable intended startup/attachment in both orientations, component stress within reviewed limits, no unexplained oscillation/latching or source instability. Allowed external capacitance and any source-specific restriction must be explicitly established before release; absent evidence remains unqualified. Rationale: steady-state success does not cover inrush, cable dynamics or transient loads.

### Step 8: controlled overload, sustained-short behavior and recovery

Energized overload and short testing is blocked until an engineer reviews the exact TPS2065CDBVR fault/thermal/recovery sections and approves the fixture, source/cable capability, current/energy/time limits, temperature/junction estimate, emergency cutoff and sample disposition. Use attended energy-limited tests, establish safe pulse limits before increasing duration, and stop on any exceeded limit or inconclusive source clipping. Static IOS 1.2-1.9 A is not an instantaneous cap; no indefinite-short or automatic-recovery claim is allowed without exact-device evidence and measured results.

Before H4, retrieve and review the exact current TI TPS2065C datasheet and orderable DBVR information linked in docs/BOM.md, including applicability conditions, current-limit behavior, transient response, thermal shutdown/restart, disabled-output discharge and fault-removal recovery. Extract section/page/revision and actual limits; this planning stage has not refreshed those sources or closed that review. Do not reuse MIC2544 foldback/cycling statements, TPS2051C ratings or TPS2065C-2 behavior. If recovery or safe test limits remain ambiguous, keep the test blocked and seek technical clarification through an authorized route.

Review source compliance and delivered fault energy, including input capacitors, cable inductance and fixture parasitics. The 1.9 A static upper limit gives an instantaneous 5.25 V x 1.9 A scale of about 9.98 W; normal-load dissipation cannot justify a sustained short. Ensure the load/short switch, shunt, connectors, wires, probes and cutoff are rated for the reviewed transient case. Define hard abort temperature, energy and duration limits using the weakest part/fixture rating plus uncertainty and a justified U1 junction-temperature model; if those are not established, do not energize. Establish a safe short pulse first, inspect/cool, then increase duration only within a preapproved energy envelope. A preselected sequence such as 10 ms, 100 ms and 1 s is only a proposal to evaluate after that review, not permission to run it or evidence it is safe. Sustained intervals and repetition counts require their own reviewed thermal justification.

Use a dedicated characterized sample and an attended, guarded remotely actuated short fixture. Characterize overload onset/current-limit spread while keeping the other connector's total loading known. Apply the reviewed fault independently at J2 and at J3; monitor VBUS_RAW, +5V_PROTECTED, both connector voltages, current and LED state. They share one protection domain; loss of the other output/LED during a fault is expected common-rail impact, not evidence of channel isolation. Repeat exact approved conditions at input extremes/ambient corners as justified by the thermal review. Record transient overshoot and static limiting only when the measurement and source have adequate headroom and bandwidth.

For sustained-short characterization record full current/voltage/temperature-versus-time, any shutdown/cycling and source interaction. A cycle is an observation to compare with exact-device evidence, not automatically a pass. On fault removal, observe recovery without adding an EN drive or assuming a particular retry mechanism; record whether recovery is autonomous or requires a documented permitted source cycle and whether it matches the exact-device contract. Recheck unloaded current, 500 mA delivery, LED and visual/mechanical damage after cooling. Quarantine fault-stressed samples from general use until reviewed.

Acceptance: current-limit behavior and recovery agree with exact-device conditions; stresses stay within the reviewed safe test envelope; the tested sustained duration shows no damage or uncontrolled heat; normal function and strict idle budget are retained afterward. Report the exact duration, repetitions, samples, source and ambient scope. Never extrapolate this to a safe indefinite short, guaranteed instantaneous ceiling or untested production variation. Rationale: a common active limiter needs measured board-level fault and recovery evidence, with bounded energy rather than an unlimited short experiment.

### Step 9: review, corrective changes and release decision

Reconcile every result with requirements and ledger assumptions. Record failures without rewriting limits after seeing data. Any replacement component, resistor value, connector, copper/plane, hole or source-contract change requires a documented proposal, affected-doc/constraint updates, actual ERC/DRC/drift/pin/footprint/legibility gates as applicable and source-bound export regeneration. No board changes are made by this plan. Review PCB return topology and bypass loop improvements before next revision; adding zones requires a supported fill-validation path because the current exporter cannot accept unvalidated fills.

Archive raw traces, photos, calibration/uncertainty and signed conclusions beside the tested revision. The original eight software stages can finish while H0-H5 hardware release work remains open. Obtain a separate explicit decision before additional manufacture, procurement or external sharing. Rationale: a repeatable engineering record must preserve both successes and remaining unknowns.

## 6. Acceptance/evidence tracking matrix

All physical and procurement entries below are NOT RUN or OPEN. Do not mark a row passed merely because this plan exists.

## 7. Risk register and next owner action

| Risk / consequence | Evidence and mitigation required | Proposed owner / priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Four intrinsic J1 hole_clearance errors | Raw 0.1944 versus 0.2500 mm; exact GCT drawing, NPTH/slot registration and fabrication process review; supported correction/disposition and rerun checks before order | PCB/library reviewer + fabricator; fabrication HOLD |
| J3 hole fit and unkeyed polarity | Finished plated holes 0.97-1.07 mm, not ordinary nominal drill tolerance; inspect mating/insertion, labels and strain relief | Mechanical/PCB reviewer; fabrication/assembly HOLD |
| Manual assembly and connector access | J1 exposed fine-pitch row/anchors; U1 five leads; LED heating limits and process caveat; J2 screw torque support; exact drawing overlays and trial process | Assembly reviewer; first-power HOLD |
| Conditional idle-current evidence | U1 LED-loaded bias reserve and both leakage allocations remain unproven; range-wide uncertainty-aware tests and source evidence; maintain strict <2 mA | Electrical reviewer; qualification HOLD |
| LED may be too dim | 2 mA optical data does not cover intended low current; characterize minimum input/viewing; revise only with budget rerun | Electrical/requirements owner; qualification HOLD |
| Source entitlement/startup/capacitors | Rd alone is not current negotiation; validate capable source/cable and effective capacitance including DC bias/aging | Electrical reviewer; power/fault HOLD |
| Shared rail and severe faults | 1.2-1.9 A static limit, dynamic overshoot unknown; exact TI thermal/recovery review and energy-limited tests; both outputs/LED collapse together | Electrical/test reviewer; fault HOLD |
| Draft returns, necks/vias and thermal area | Long routed ground returns, no plane, 0.8 mm trunks and smaller escapes are unqualified; calculate/measure drop/heating and redesign if needed | PCB/power reviewer; qualification HOLD |
| Backfeed / parallel supplies | Reverse blocking not specified; outputs are loads only; fixture must not source current; add no unsupported operating mode | Bench operator; every energized step |
| Cost and availability | USD 2.5439 Q100 estimate contains J2 USD 0.590 Q1-only estimate; Harwin snapshot only 5 stock/22-week lead time; obtain current exact quotes | Sourcing/project owner; ordering HOLD |
| Misleading metadata or export interpretation | Use exact TPS2065CDBVR identity; fix inheritance before library reuse. Gerber stroke bounds 40.1 x 30.1 are not authorized board enlargement; DXF inch scaling and entities need review | Library/CAM reviewer; reuse/fabrication HOLD |
| False qualification from software/small samples | Native gates do not remove raw J1 findings or establish measured compliance; sample/corner data do not cover all process/aging/ESD/EMC conditions | Project/release reviewer; final release HOLD |

Rationale: each known uncertainty has a concrete next action and a hold point rather than a generic warning.

## 8. Prototype order plan, for review only

ASSUMED planning batch only: request a quotation for five bare PCBs and exact components for three assemblies, assemble one first, and reserve the other boards for repeat/corner and controlled fault work. Do not place an order, upload a package for manufacture, approve substitutions or spend money from this plan. ### Quote and CAM checklist

1. Request current exact-MPN quantity-3/6 prices and lead times for this small batch, and a separate Q100-board component quote: 100 of each single-per-board line and 200 each of the 5.1k resistors and capacitors. Do not multiply Q100 unit prices to pretend they are a small-batch quotation. Current Q100 estimate is USD 2.5439 per board, with the explicitly uncertain J2 line and unverified availability; no supplier guarantee exists.
2. Ask for five bare, two-layer boards, 1 oz copper, nominal 1.6 mm FR-4 and intended finished outline <=40 x 30 mm, subject to confirmed fabrication tolerances and no mandatory holes/enclosure. Quote copper/plating and finished-hole controls, especially J3 0.97-1.07 mm, J1 NPTH/PTH registration, drill/slot interpretation, masks/silkscreen and actual connector edge geometry. No generic online default is accepted as evidence of those constraints.
3. Use only the reviewed current generated outputs/jlcpcb.zip and its source-bound manifest, separate PTH/NPTH drills and Gerbers. The current profile is jlcpcb-kicad9-2026-09-24 / KiCad 9.0.2 with no copper zones; this identifies the export settings, not an accepted manufacturer order. Review the job metadata's 0.100 mm plotted outline stroke versus 40 x 30 mm centerline and finished-edge tolerances. For DXF, confirm the documented inch scaling and whether hole/slot entities should be imported. Inspect actual CAM previews, front/back SVG and STEP before approving manufacture; generation alone is not inspection.
4. Have the PCB/library reviewer and fabricator explicitly address all four J1 findings and exact component land/drawing correspondence. If changes are needed, revise through the validated workflow, rerun original checks and regenerate the entire bound export package. No manual edit of the ZIP, manifest or rule suppressions to obtain a pass.
5. Assemble the approval request with seller/provider, exact quantities and revisions, all fabrication/assembly options, itemized components/PCB/assembly/tooling/spares, shipping/taxes, currency and total landed cost, payment method, delivery address/method and promised lead time, and visible cancellation/return restrictions. Share ordinary personal delivery details only with the specifically approved provider for the approved order. Obtain explicit user approval before upload/submission/payment where applicable; this plan is not that approval.
6. After a separately approved order, record real order identifiers, purchased quantities, actual invoice/lead times and eventual receiving inspection. Until then keep all procurement fields blank or NOT ORDERED. Do not invent a purchase, tracking number or delivery date.

The <USD 8 Q100 requirement covers all fitted components but excludes PCB fabrication, assembly, shipping and tax. The prototype approval total must include those real costs separately. A low estimated BOM does not imply a small total order or authorize spending.

Rationale: a complete order plan can be ready for review without transmitting the package, selecting substitutions or committing money.

## 9. Run-sheet template and completion rule

For each Pxx test record: board/revision and date; prerequisite hold signoffs; source/cable/fixture; exact conditions and instrument uncertainty; expected criterion fixed before run; actual raw file/photo links and numerical results; PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE / NOT RUN; anomaly and stop reason; reviewer and required retest. Keep a separate change log for rework. The current values for every physical actual-result field are NOT RUN; no signoff, waveform or measured temperature exists yet.

The software deliverable is this reviewed plan, its synchronized specification reference and the actual original gate outcome. The physical deliverable remains unbuilt and unqualified. Preserve the real firmware NOT APPLICABLE outcome and every original stage; do not replace hardware validation with a fabricated software build.

Count every VBUS-fed path once; measure source-CC demand separately. The 0.831 mA ledger remains conditional. Corner/sample tests alone do not prove all temperature, tolerance, aging or production extremes; close the remaining range-wide analysis and evidence before qualification.

Energized overload and short testing is blocked until an engineer reviews the exact TPS2065CDBVR fault/thermal/recovery sections and approves the fixture, source/cable capability, current/energy/time limits, temperature/junction estimate, emergency cutoff and sample disposition. Use attended energy-limited tests, establish safe pulse limits before increasing duration, and stop on any exceeded limit or inconclusive source clipping. Static IOS 1.2-1.9 A is not an instantaneous cap; no indefinite-short or automatic-recovery claim is allowed without exact-device evidence and measured results.
